messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: sustained TPM spike on model-family 'aurora-7b' ➜ 3x baseline for 12m. Latency 95p rising, GPU pool autoscaler saturated.
Diego: I'm taking this. Observing queued requests and rising p50->p95 gap. Likely hot prefix /chat endpoint.
Sam: Any visible customer errors yet? 429s or 503s?
Tariq: A few 429s from high-volume customers, mainly sandbox/dev keys. 503s minimal. Errors correlate with <long_instruction> prompts.
Diego: Plan: surgical per-model quota reduction for aurora family to stop downstream queuing. Start with TPM -> 80% of current and RPM -> 70%, apply canary to non-prod first, then prod carveout if green. Also disable streaming for aurora-7b for 10m as fallback.
Emily: +1. Can we do per-route shaping too (chat vs generate)? Chat is heavier.
Diego: yes. Order of ops: 1) canary quota change to prod-us-west gating traffic 2) monitor latency & 5xxs 3) widen to all regions 4) rollback if regressions.
Sam: How about targeted customer throttles instead of broad family cut? We have one heavy tenant using aurora-7b with bursty traffic.
Diego: Good call. We'll add two steps in parallel: carve out heavy tenant (customer-id = cust-4023) with explicit throttle, and reduce family-wide TPM. If carveout suffices, we'll relax family cut.
Diego: Executing canary now. Command:```
redwoodctl quota set --model aurora-7b --tpm 220 --rpm 120 --scope prod-us-west --reason "live mitigation - traffic surge"
```
deploy-bot: ACCEPTED: quota update queued (job id: q-87921). Applying to prod-us-west canary nodes. ETA ~30s.
Diego: Also applying tenant carveout:```
redwoodctl customer-throttle set --customer cust-4023 --model-family aurora --tpm 40 --rpm 30 --note "temporary burst control"
```
deploy-bot: APPLIED: customer throttle set for cust-4023.
Tariq: Metrics update: after canary apply p95 latency down 18%, queued requests down 40% in canary region. No new 5xxs observed. Some 429s still from cust-4023 before throttle applied.
Ava (support): We're seeing support tickets from 2 customers: cust-104 / cust-209 reporting intermittent 429s. I flagged them and sent canned note.
Sam: For customers that see 429s during carveout, recommend temporary guidance: retry backoff 1s jitter, and mention we're actively mitigating.
Emily: Re KV/prefix caching — aurora has low cache hit for the hot prefixes. Any chance to enable aggressive KV caching for 5m windows?
Diego: We can flip prefix cache policy for aurora on canary nodes. Doing:```
redwoodctl cache update --model aurora-7b --prefix-cache-ttl 300 --scope prod-us-west
```
deploy-bot: CACHE CHANGE APPLIED to canary.
Tariq: Observed cache hit rate jumped from 12% -> 47% in canary, token generation CPU usage down 20%. Latency improved further.
Diego: Good. Escalating family cut to all regions with slightly softer numbers to reduce customer pain:```
redwoodctl quota set --model-family aurora --tpm 240 --rpm 140 --scope global --reason "escalate mitigation after successful canary"
```
deploy-bot: GLOBAL QUOTA JOB ACCEPTED (q-87925). Rolling to regions in waves.
Tariq: Rolling update status: us-west -> ok, eu-west -> in progress, ap-southeast -> pending. Early eu-west metrics look similar to canary improvements.
Ava (support): Crafting status update for affected customers, calling out that degraded throughput may produce short 429s and recommending retries. Will attach ETA ~15-30m for full resolution.
Sam: Any concern about model fidelity/regression after cache/policy flips? Need to document for product/ML.
Diego: Small chance for slight token timing differences but no prompt->completion quality regressions expected. We'll snapshot a couple of prompt sets and run quick evals once roll completes. Emily, can you kick off eval job?
Emily: On it. Running the quick prompt-set against aurora-7b and aurora-7b-quant variants. ETA 12m.
Tariq: Note: autoscaler still flagging a pool at 92% GPU mem for a tiny subset of pods — investigating whether older model variant spawned heavy KV misses.
Diego: If pods saturate, we'll move remaining traffic to fallback model small-aurora-3b until autoscaler relieves. Adding fallback route now.```
redwoodctl route update --from model-family aurora --fallback small-aurora-3b --threshold 80
```
deploy-bot: ROUTE UPDATE APPLIED.
Tariq: After fallback rule, immediate reduction in queue length for the stressed pool. Good.
Diego: Summary: canary quotas + tenant throttle + prefix cache tweak + global family throttle + fallback route applied. Impact: transient 429s for a small subset of customers (mostly high-burst dev keys). No broad customer data loss, latency improved.
Ava (support): Created support incident INC-2145, added customers cust-104, cust-209, cust-4023. Sending proactive emails.
Sam: Next steps: 1) keep mitigation for 30m, 2) analyze logs for root cause (hot prefixes, workload type), 3) consider permanent routing/policy for heavy dev tenants or stricter sandbox limits.
Diego: I'll monitor for 40m then hand off to next on-call. If things stabilize, we'll relax family TPM by 10% increments.
incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff scheduled to @Diego -> @next-oncall at 2145682200.
Diego: Handoff: leave quotas as-is for now. Next on-call please keep an eye on queue length and 95p latency. I'll attach the quick eval results and the commands used in the incident doc.
Emily: Eval finished: no significant quality degradation detected. Attaching minimal diff summary to thread.
Ava (support): Will follow up with affected customers after mitigation fully lifts.
Diego: Wrapping up. If anyone sees regression or new 5xxs, ping both me and @next-oncall immediately. :thumbsup:
